title: U.S. House · Wisconsin's 4th Congressional District
area: The city of Milwaukee and near suburbs.

context.text: Incumbent Gwen Moore (D) defeated Amy Donahue 70.5%-29.3% in the Democratic primary. Tim Rogers advanced from the Republican primary. Arthur Burks also qualified as an independent for the general-election ballot; two other independents, Carlos Dixon and Robert Raymond, withdrew or were disqualified.

candidates.name: Gwen Moore
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Amy Donahue 70.5%-29.3% in the Democratic primary.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 4th Congressional District (since 2005)

summary.text: Gwen Moore is the Democratic incumbent representing Wisconsin's 4th District (Milwaukee), a seat she has held since 2005. A former state legislator, she serves on the House Ways and Means Committee.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Marquette University in 1978 and became a housing officer for the Wisconsin Housing Development Authority.
Served in the Wisconsin State Assembly from 1989 to 1992 and the Wisconsin State Senate from 1993 to 2003 before her election to Congress.

record.text: Serves on the Joint Economic Committee and the House Committee on Ways and Means (Social Security, Tax, and Work and Welfare subcommittees) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.researchNotes: Her official website lists issue areas (economy and jobs, health care, immigration, environment, veterans, among others) but no extractable position statements were found as of the research date.

candidates.name: Tim Rogers

summary.text: Tim Rogers is a Milwaukee resident and delivery worker running as the Republican nominee for Wisconsin's 4th Congressional District.

background.text: Born and lives in Milwaukee, Wisconsin; graduated from North Division High School in 1978 and studied at the University of Wisconsin-Parkside and Milwaukee Area Technical College.
Career experience includes working as a delivery person.

candidates.researchNotes: Rogers has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and no current campaign website statements on issues were found as of the research date.

candidates.name: Arthur Burks

summary.text: Arthur Burks is an independent candidate on the general-election ballot for Wisconsin's 4th Congressional District.
